				<div id="mw-content-text" class="mw-body-content"><div class="mw-content-ltr mw-parser-output" lang="en" dir="ltr"><table align="center" style="margin: 3px auto; background: rgb(250, 255, 244); border: 2px solid rgb(145, 81, 33); border-radius: 40px;">

<td style="background:#B88E6F; padding: 10px; border-radius: 40px; -moz-border-radius: 40px; -webkit-border-radius: 40px; -khtml-border-radius: 40px; -icab-border-radius: 40px; -o-border-radius: 40px;;" width="50px" align="center"><span typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:0050Diglett.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/a/a6/0050Diglett.png/50px-0050Diglett.png" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="50" height="50" class="mw-file-element" srcset="https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/a/a6/0050Diglett.png/75px-0050Diglett.png 1.5x, https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/a/a6/0050Diglett.png/100px-0050Diglett.png 2x" data-file-width="758" data-file-height="758"></a></span>
</td>
<td style="padding-left:3px; padding-right:20px"><b>This article is incomplete.</b><br>Please feel free to edit this article to add missing information and complete it. <br><small>Reason: Needs more information on spin-off games</small>

<dl><dd><i>This article is about the random event. For the video podcast, see <a href="/wiki/It%27s_Super_Effective_(podcast)#Related_podcasts" title="It's Super Effective (podcast)">It's Super Effective (podcast) → Related podcasts</a>.</i></dd></dl>
<figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Rinto_Gallade_critical_hit.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/f/f8/Rinto_Gallade_critical_hit.png/250px-Rinto_Gallade_critical_hit.png" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="250" height="141" class="mw-file-element" srcset="https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/f/f8/Rinto_Gallade_critical_hit.png/375px-Rinto_Gallade_critical_hit.png 1.5x, https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/f/f8/Rinto_Gallade_critical_hit.png/500px-Rinto_Gallade_critical_hit.png 2x" data-file-width="1280" data-file-height="720"></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Rinto" title="Rinto">Rinto</a>'s <a href="/wiki/Gallade_(Pok%C3%A9mon)" title="Gallade (Pokémon)">Gallade</a> taking a critical hit from <a href="/wiki/Fury_Cutter_(move)" title="Fury Cutter (move)">Fury Cutter</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>A <b>critical hit</b> (Japanese: <b><ruby lang="ja">急所<rp>(</rp><rt>きゅうしょ</rt><rp>)</rp></ruby></b> <i><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/pressure_point" class="extiw" title="wp:pressure point">pressure point</a></i>) is a (generally) random event that multiplies the <a href="/wiki/Damage" title="Damage">damage</a> of a damage-dealing <a href="/wiki/Move" title="Move">move</a>. 
</p><p>When one occurs, the game will display the message "A critical hit!" (Japanese: <ruby lang="ja">急所<rp>(</rp><rt>きゅうしょ</rt><rp>)</rp></ruby>に　<ruby lang="ja">当<rp>(</rp><rt>あ</rt><rp>)</rp></ruby>たった！| <i>Hit a pressure point!</i>), or just "Critical hit!" in <a href="/wiki/Generation_I" title="Generation I">Generation I</a>, after the damage is dealt. Starting with <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Omega_Ruby_and_Alpha_Sapphire" title="Pokémon Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire">Pokémon Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire</a> (except for <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Legends:_Arceus" title="Pokémon Legends: Arceus">Pokémon Legends: Arceus</a>), this message is displayed in special color (with the specific color varying between bright yellow, orange, and golden yellow depending on the game).
</p>

Muted</div></div></div></div></div></div><h2><span class="mw-headline" id="In_the_core_series_games">In the core series games</span></h2>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Generation_I">Generation I</span></h3>
<h4><span class="mw-headline" id="Damage">Damage</span></h4>
<p>When a move lands a critical hit, the attacker's level will be doubled during <a href="/wiki/Damage" title="Damage">damage</a> calculation. A rough approximation for the damage multiplier is <math class="mwe-math-element" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mstyle displaystyle="false" scriptlevel="0"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mfrac><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mn>2</mn><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></mrow><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mstyle></mrow></math> where <math class="mwe-math-element" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mstyle displaystyle="false" scriptlevel="0"><mi>L</mi></mstyle></mrow></math> is the attacker's level; as a result, lower-leveled Pokémon have a smaller critical hit boost than higher-leveled Pokémon. For example, a level 5 Pokémon will inflict about 1.5× damage on a critical hit, while a level 20 Pokémon will inflict 1.8× and a level 95 Pokémon will inflict 1.95×.
</p><p>Critical hits use the attacker and defender's original <a href="/wiki/Stat" title="Stat">stats</a> with no modifications. This means it is possible for a critical hit to deal less damage than a non-critical hit if the attacker's stat modifications were high enough and the defender's were low enough. If the player's Pokémon has <a href="/wiki/Transform_(move)" title="Transform (move)">transformed</a>, its untransformed stats will be used (but enemies use the stats of their transformation).<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div id="AdThrive_Content_1_desktop" class="adthrive-ad adthrive-content adthrive-content-1 adthrive-ad-cls" style="min-height: 250px; align-content: start;" data-google-query-id="CPGIl6_G9pYDFfYWzAQdDdAN3g"><div id="google_ads_iframe_/18190176,1027503/AdThrive_Content_1/630428a76245162875c78210_0__container__" style="border: 0pt;"><iframe id="google_ads_iframe_/18190176,1027503/AdThrive_Content_1/630428a76245162875c78210_0" name="google_ads_iframe_/18190176,1027503/AdThrive_Content_1/630428a76245162875c78210_0" title="3rd party ad content" width="1" height="1" scrolling="no" marginwidth="0" marginheight="0" frameborder="0" aria-label="Advertisement" tabindex="0" allow="private-state-token-redemption" data-load-complete="true" data-google-container-id="1" style="border: 0px; vertical-align: bottom;"></iframe></div></div><h4><span class="mw-headline" id="Probability">Probability</span></h4>
<dl><dd><i>Main article: <a href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Pok%C3%A9mon_by_critical_hit_rate_in_Generation_I&action=edit&redlink=1" class="new" title="List of Pokémon by critical hit rate in Generation I (page does not exist)">List of Pokémon by critical hit rate in Generation I</a></i></dd></dl>
<p>Whether a move scores a critical hit is determined by comparing a 1-byte random number (0 to 255) against a 1-byte threshold value (also 0 to 255). If the random number is strictly less than the threshold, the Pokémon scores a critical hit. For a given threshold value <math class="mwe-math-element" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mstyle displaystyle="true" scriptlevel="0"><mi>T</mi></mstyle></mrow></math>, the probability of scoring a critical hit is <math class="mwe-math-element" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mstyle displaystyle="false" scriptlevel="0"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mfrac><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>T</mi></mrow><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn><mn>6</mn></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mstyle></mrow></math>. If the threshold would exceed 255, it instead becomes 255. Consequently, the maximum possible chance of landing a critical hit is 255/256. (If the generated random number is 255, that number can never be less than the threshold, regardless of the value of the threshold.)
</p><p>In the Generation I core series games, the threshold is normally equal to half the user's <a href="/wiki/Base_stats" title="Base stats">base</a> <a href="/wiki/Stat#Speed" title="Stat">Speed</a>. If the move used has a high critical-hit ratio (<a href="/wiki/Crabhammer_(move)" title="Crabhammer (move)">Crabhammer</a>, <a href="/wiki/Karate_Chop_(move)" title="Karate Chop (move)">Karate Chop</a>, <a href="/wiki/Razor_Leaf_(move)" title="Razor Leaf (move)">Razor Leaf</a>, or <a href="/wiki/Slash_(move)" title="Slash (move)">Slash</a>), the move is 8 times more likely to be a critical hit (up to a maximum of 255/256). If the Pokémon has used <a href="/wiki/Focus_Energy_(move)" title="Focus Energy (move)">Focus Energy</a> or a <a href="/wiki/Dire_Hit" title="Dire Hit">Dire Hit</a>, due to a bug, the user is 1/4 as likely to land a critical hit.
</p><p>The threshold has the following values, depending on the move used and whether the user is under the effect of Focus Energy or a Dire Hit. The probability of landing a critical hit is simply these values divided by 256.
</p>

<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Generation_II_onwards">Generation II onwards</span></h3>
<h4><span class="mw-headline" id="Damage_2">Damage</span></h4>
<p>From Generation <a href="/wiki/Generation_II" title="Generation II">II</a> to <a href="/wiki/Generation_V" title="Generation V">V</a>, a critical hit deals 2 times the normal damage. From Generation <a href="/wiki/Generation_VI" title="Generation VI">VI</a> onward, a critical hit deals 1.5 times the normal damage.
</p><p>In Generation II, when a move scores a critical hit, all stat stage modifiers, the halved Attack from burn, and the defensive boosts from screens (<a href="/wiki/Light_Screen_(move)" title="Light Screen (move)">Light Screen</a> and <a href="/wiki/Reflect_(move)" title="Reflect (move)">Reflect</a>) are ignored if the target's defending stat stage (<a href="/wiki/Stat#Defense" title="Stat">Defense</a> or <a href="/wiki/Stat#Special_Defense" title="Stat">Special Defense</a>) is greater than or equal to the attacker's attacking stat stage (<a href="/wiki/Stat#Attack" title="Stat">Attack</a> or <a href="/wiki/Stat#Special_Attack" title="Stat">Special Attack</a>).
</p><p>From <a href="/wiki/Generation_III" title="Generation III">Generation III</a> onward, when a move scores a critical hit, the attacker's negative stat stages, the defender's positive stat stages, and the defensive boosts from <a href="/wiki/Category:Screen-creating_moves" title="Category:Screen-creating moves">screens</a> are always ignored. However, the halved damage from physical moves due to a burn is no longer ignored.
</p>
<dl><dt>Examples</dt></dl>
<ul><li>If the attacker is using a <a href="/wiki/Physical_move" title="Physical move">physical move</a> and is at +2 Attack stages while the target is at +1 Defense stage...
<ul><li>Gen II: a critical hit will not ignore either stat. (Damage with a critical hit will have an 8/3× modifier.)</li>
<li>Gen III-V: a critical hit will ignore the Defense boost. (Damage with a critical hit will have a 4× modifier.)</li>
<li>Gen VI+: a critical hit will ignore the Defense boost. (Damage with a critical hit will have a 3× modifier.)</li></ul></li>
<li>If the attacker is using a <a href="/wiki/Physical_move" title="Physical move">physical move</a> and is at -1 Attack stages while the target is at -2 Defense stage...
<ul><li>Gen II: a critical hit will not ignore either stat. (Damage with a critical hit will have a 2.64× modifier.)</li>
<li>Gen III-V: a critical hit will ignore the Attack drop. (Damage with a critical hit will have a 4× modifier.)</li>
<li>Gen VI+: a critical hit will ignore the Attack drop. (Damage with a critical hit will have a 3× modifier.)</li></ul></li></ul>
<h4><span class="mw-headline" id="Other_effects">Other effects</span></h4>
<p>If a Pokémon with the <a href="/wiki/Sniper_(Ability)" title="Sniper (Ability)">Sniper</a> Ability gets a critical hit, the damage dealt will be multiplied by an additional factor of 1.5.
</p><p>If <a href="/wiki/Galarian_form" title="Galarian form">Galarian</a> <a href="/wiki/Farfetch%27d_(Pok%C3%A9mon)" title="Farfetch'd (Pokémon)">Farfetch'd</a> lands at least three critical hits in a single battle, it <a href="/wiki/Evolution" title="Evolution">evolves</a> into <a href="/wiki/Sirfetch%27d_(Pok%C3%A9mon)" title="Sirfetch'd (Pokémon)">Sirfetch'd</a> at the end of the battle.
</p>
<h4><span class="mw-headline" id="Probability_2">Probability</span></h4>
<p>The probability of landing a critical hit is no longer based on the attacker's base Speed, but rather is based on a fixed formula for all Pokémon. Similar to <a href="/wiki/Stat" title="Stat">stats</a>, there are temporary in-battle stages used to determine the probability that a particular move will be a critical hit.
</p>

<h5><span class="mw-headline" id="Moves_that_cannot_score_a_critical_hit">Moves that cannot score a critical hit</span></h5>
<p>In some early battles, the games prevent all moves from scoring critical hits:
</p>
<ul><li>In <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Ruby_and_Sapphire_Versions" title="Pokémon Ruby and Sapphire Versions">Pokémon Ruby, Sapphire</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Emerald_Version" title="Pokémon Emerald Version">Emerald</a>, during the first battle with <a href="/wiki/Poochyena_(Pok%C3%A9mon)" title="Poochyena (Pokémon)">Poochyena</a><b><sup class="noexcerpt"><a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Ruby_and_Sapphire_Versions" title="Pokémon Ruby and Sapphire Versions"><span style="color:#CD2236;">R</span></a></sup></b><b><sup class="noexcerpt"><a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Ruby_and_Sapphire_Versions" title="Pokémon Ruby and Sapphire Versions"><span style="color:#3D51A7;">S</span></a></sup></b>/<a href="/wiki/Zigzagoon_(Pok%C3%A9mon)" title="Zigzagoon (Pokémon)">Zigzagoon</a><b><sup class="noexcerpt"><a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Emerald_Version" title="Pokémon Emerald Version"><span style="color:#009652;">E</span></a></sup></b>.</li>
<li>In <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Diamond_and_Pearl_Versions" title="Pokémon Diamond and Pearl Versions">Pokémon Diamond and Pearl</a>, during the first battle with <a href="/wiki/Starly_(Pok%C3%A9mon)" title="Starly (Pokémon)">Starly</a> at <a href="/wiki/Lake_Verity" title="Lake Verity">Lake Verity</a>.</li>
<li>In <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Platinum_Version" title="Pokémon Platinum Version">Pokémon Platinum</a>, during the first battle with <a href="/wiki/Barry_(game)" title="Barry (game)">Barry</a>.</li>
<li>In <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Scarlet_and_Violet" title="Pokémon Scarlet and Violet">Pokémon Scarlet and Violet</a>, during the first battle with <a href="/wiki/Nemona" title="Nemona">Nemona</a>.</li></ul>
<p>Generations II and III introduced a handful of moves that cannot score a critical hit. They are denoted by the ✘ symbol in the table below.
</p><p>Starting in Generation V, all damaging moves, except <a href="/wiki/Category:Moves_that_deal_direct_damage" title="Category:Moves that deal direct damage">moves that deal direct damage</a> and confusion damage, can score a critical hit.
</p>

<h5><span class="mw-headline" id="Other_factors">Other factors</span></h5>
<p>The Abilities <a href="/wiki/Battle_Armor_(Ability)" title="Battle Armor (Ability)">Battle Armor</a> and <a href="/wiki/Shell_Armor_(Ability)" title="Shell Armor (Ability)">Shell Armor</a> prevent Pokémon from landing critical hits on the Pokémon with that Ability. <a href="/wiki/Lucky_Chant_(move)" title="Lucky Chant (move)">Lucky Chant</a> prevents Pokémon from landing critical hits on the Pokémon it is protecting for a span of five turns.
</p><p>Pokémon with the Ability <a href="/wiki/Merciless_(Ability)" title="Merciless (Ability)">Merciless</a> will always score critical hits on <a href="/wiki/Poison_(status_condition)" title="Poison (status condition)">poisoned</a> Pokémon (unless prevented by one of the above effects).
</p><p>The moves <a href="/wiki/Storm_Throw_(move)" title="Storm Throw (move)">Storm Throw</a>, <a href="/wiki/Frost_Breath_(move)" title="Frost Breath (move)">Frost Breath</a>, <a href="/wiki/Zippy_Zap_(move)" title="Zippy Zap (move)">Zippy Zap</a>, <a href="/wiki/Surging_Strikes_(move)" title="Surging Strikes (move)">Surging Strikes</a>, <a href="/wiki/Wicked_Blow_(move)" title="Wicked Blow (move)">Wicked Blow</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Flower_Trick_(move)" title="Flower Trick (move)">Flower Trick</a>, along with any move used by a Pokémon that is under the effect of <a href="/wiki/Laser_Focus_(move)" title="Laser Focus (move)">Laser Focus</a>, will always result in a critical hit (unless prevented by one of the above effects).
</p><p>In <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Legends:_Z-A" title="Pokémon Legends: Z-A">Pokémon Legends: Z-A</a>, a move that lands a sneak attack on an opposing Trainer's Pokémon in the <a href="/wiki/Z-A_Royale" title="Z-A Royale">Z-A Royale</a> or a <a href="/wiki/Hyperspace" class="mw-redirect" title="Hyperspace">Hyperspace</a> battle zone will always result in a critical hit. Additionally, the move <a href="/wiki/First_Impression_(move)" title="First Impression (move)">First Impression</a> always results in a critical hit if used as a <a href="/wiki/Plus_Move" title="Plus Move">Plus Move</a>.
</p><p>Moves with increased critical-hit ratio are granted a further increase by 1 stage when performed in the <a href="/wiki/Move_mastery" title="Move mastery">strong style</a>.
</p>
<div id="AdThrive_Content_2_desktop" class="adthrive-ad adthrive-content adthrive-content-2 adthrive-ad-cls" style="min-height: 250px;"></div><h2><span class="mw-headline" id="In_the_side_series_games">In the side series games</span></h2>
<p>In the <a href="/wiki/Side_series" title="Side series">side series</a> games, the critical hit mechanics generally work as in the <a href="/wiki/Core_series" title="Core series">core series</a> games, except when otherwise stated.
</p>
<h3><span id="Pok.C3.A9mon_Stadium"></span><span class="mw-headline" id="Pokémon_Stadium">Pokémon Stadium</span></h3>
<h4><span class="mw-headline" id="Probability_3">Probability</span></h4>
<p>In <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Stadium" title="Pokémon Stadium">Pokémon Stadium</a>, the probability threshold is normally equal to 19 plus one quarter of the user's <a href="/wiki/Base_stats" title="Base stats">base</a> <a href="/wiki/Stat#Speed" title="Stat">Speed</a>. If the move used has a high critical-hit ratio (<a href="/wiki/Crabhammer_(move)" title="Crabhammer (move)">Crabhammer</a>, <a href="/wiki/Karate_Chop_(move)" title="Karate Chop (move)">Karate Chop</a>, <a href="/wiki/Razor_Leaf_(move)" title="Razor Leaf (move)">Razor Leaf</a>, or <a href="/wiki/Slash_(move)" title="Slash (move)">Slash</a>), the move is 8 times more likely to be a critical hit (up to a maximum of 255/256). If the Pokémon has used <a href="/wiki/Focus_Energy_(move)" title="Focus Energy (move)">Focus Energy</a> or a <a href="/wiki/Dire_Hit" title="Dire Hit">Dire Hit</a>, the user is more likely to land a critical hit (the exact increase is slightly complicated).
</p><p>The threshold has the following values, depending on the move used and whether the user is under the effect of Focus Energy or a Dire Hit. The probability of landing a critical hit is simply these values divided by 256.
</p><p>In Pokémon Stadium, the threshold value <i>T</i> is determined by a different formula. If <i>T</i> would exceed 255, its value instead becomes exactly 255.
</p>

<h3><span id="Pok.C3.A9mon_Colosseum"></span><span class="mw-headline" id="Pokémon_Colosseum">Pokémon Colosseum</span></h3>
<p>In <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Colosseum" title="Pokémon Colosseum">Pokémon Colosseum</a>, the move <a href="/wiki/Shadow_Rush_(move)" title="Shadow Rush (move)">Shadow Rush</a> has an additional 90% chance to land a critical hit when the user is in <a href="/wiki/Hyper_Mode" title="Hyper Mode">Hyper Mode</a>. Failing that, it has the usual 6.25% chance to land a critical hit regardless, for overall a total of a 90.625% chance to land a critical hit.
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="In_the_spin-off_games">In the spin-off games</span></h2>
<h3><span id="Pok.C3.A9mon_Mystery_Dungeon_series"></span><span class="mw-headline" id="Pokémon_Mystery_Dungeon_series">Pokémon Mystery Dungeon series</span></h3>
<h4><span class="mw-headline" id="Rescue_Team_and_Explorers">Rescue Team and Explorers</span></h4>
<p>There are some differences from how critical hits work in the main series:
</p>
<ul><li>Critical hits deal only 50% more damage, unless the Pokémon has <a href="/wiki/Sniper_(Ability)" title="Sniper (Ability)">Sniper</a>, in which case it will deal double damage.</li>
<li>Male or gender unknown Pokémon will have the move's base critical hit rate multiplied by 1.5×.</li>
<li><a href="/wiki/Scope_Lens" title="Scope Lens">Scope Lens</a>, <a href="/wiki/Patsy_Band" class="mw-redirect" title="Patsy Band">Patsy Band</a>, Sharpshooter <a href="/wiki/IQ" title="IQ">IQ</a> skill and <a href="/wiki/Super_Luck_(Ability)" title="Super Luck (Ability)">Super Luck</a> add a flat modifier to the move's critical hit rate (30% in Red/Blue Rescue Team, 15% in Explorers). This can also allow the <a href="/wiki/Regular_attack" title="Regular attack">regular attack</a> to deal critical hits.</li>
<li>Type Advantage Master will set the critical hit rate to 40%, ignoring all other effects.</li>
<li>Focus Energy will guarantee critical hits, provided the critical hits are not prevented by <a href="/wiki/Exclusive_item" title="Exclusive item">exclusive items</a>, <a href="/wiki/Ability" title="Ability">Abilities</a>, Critical Dodger IQ skill, or <a href="/wiki/Lucky_Chant_(move)" title="Lucky Chant (move)">Lucky Chant</a>.</li></ul>

<h3><span id="Pok.C3.A9mon_Masters_EX"></span><span class="mw-headline" id="Pokémon_Masters_EX">Pokémon Masters EX</span></h3>
<p>Here are some notable qualities of critical hits in this game:
</p>
<ul><li>Critical-hit rate is treated as a stat like Attack or evasion, except critical-hit rate can only be raised to a maximum of three stat ranks (or to +3) and can't be lowered below 0. A few moves, such as <a href="/wiki/Snatch_(move)" title="Snatch (move)">Snatch</a>, can reset target's critical-hit rate to 0 unless that target has Steady Aim <a href="/wiki/Skill_(Masters)" title="Skill (Masters)">skill</a>.
<ul><li>Attack moves passively have their base critical-hit rates set to 0, which means that using one with its user's critical-hit rate raised to three stat ranks yields an 100% chance to land a critical hit (per target).</li>
<li>Damage-dealing sync moves and max moves have their base critical-hit rates set to -1, which means that using one with its user's critical-hit rate raised to three stat ranks normally yields an 80% chance to land a critical hit (per target).</li></ul></li>
<li>Some effects allow critical hits to land more easily [from attack moves like Slash or Spacial Rend, sync moves like Moonlight Leaf Blade, or skills like Zero In 1, Soften Up 1 (only for sync moves), Dire Rain 1, etc.].
<ul><li>Attack/Sync moves with this effect passively have their base critical-hit rates set to +1. Sync moves with this effect no longer have -1 critical hit-rate penalty.</li>
<li>Each skill with this effect is always accompanied by a one or a two, and if that skill's conditions are met, then it passively raises critical-hit rate by that number.</li></ul></li>
<li>Applying the Critical Hit Next effect on a sync pair guarantees that their next attack/sync move will be a critical hit, except in certain circumstances.</li>
<li>Critical hits do ×1.5 damage, which can be further enhanced by having Critastrophe [X] (for sync moves) or Critical Strike [Y] (for any attacks) skills; in which case, it will do even more damage by a factor of +(X × 10)% or +(Y × 10)%, respectively. (X and Y are numbers between one and nine.)
<ul><li>Multiple copies of such multipliers stack additively. For example, if a sync pair has Critical Strike 9 (+90% damage) and Critical Strike 2 (+20%), then the skills will stack to become a factor of +110% (or ×2.1).</li></ul></li>
<li>Critical hits ignore effects of physical damage reduction (from Reflect etc.) and special damage reduction (from Light Screen etc.).</li>
<li>Critical-Hit Defense effects temporarily protect all pairs in its field of play from critical hits. The move <a href="/wiki/Defog_(move)" title="Defog (move)">Defog</a> removes this effect from opposing fields of play.</li>
<li>Skills such as Vigilance protect their users from critical hits. A few moves, such as <a href="/wiki/Sunsteel_Strike_(move)" title="Sunsteel Strike (move)">Sunsteel Strike</a>, and a few skills, like Piercing Blows, bypass these effects.</li>
<li>Chances to land critical hits with attack moves, ignoring certain circumstances, are as follows:</li></ul>

<div id="AdThrive_Content_3_desktop" class="adthrive-ad adthrive-content adthrive-content-3 adthrive-ad-cls" style="min-height: 250px;"></div><h3><span id="Pok.C3.A9mon_UNITE"></span><span class="mw-headline" id="Pokémon_UNITE">Pokémon UNITE</span></h3>
<p>In <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_UNITE" title="Pokémon UNITE">Pokémon UNITE</a>, critical hits are a mechanic. It is very similar to the main series games, in that an attack that inflicts a critical hit deals double the damage to the opponent that it would normally. Critical hits are indicated by a symbol resembling a thick arrow appearing next to the damage numbers displayed by an attack, and said damage numbers appear larger than they otherwise would. 
</p><p>Some <a href="/wiki/Held_item" title="Held item">Held items</a>, <a href="/wiki/Move" title="Move">moves</a> and <a href="/wiki/Ability" title="Ability">Abilities</a>, such as the <a href="/wiki/Scope_Lens" title="Scope Lens">Scope Lens</a> and <a href="/wiki/Super_Luck_(Ability)" title="Super Luck (Ability)">Super Luck</a> can increase the chance that critical hits occur. <a href="/wiki/Huge_Power_(Ability)" title="Huge Power (Ability)">Huge Power</a> causes all attacks that hit a single opponent to be critical hits, but prevents attacks that hit multiple opponents from being critical hits.
</p><p>In the Prize Machine, a <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9_Ball#Pokémon_UNITE" title="Poké Ball">Unite Ball</a> that causes the progress meter to fill by three or five points displays the same arrow symbol by the visual of the added points, implying that this is also considered a critical hit of sorts.
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="In_animation">In animation</span></h2>
<figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Bea_Machamp_G-Max_Chi_Strike_effect.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/1/13/Bea_Machamp_G-Max_Chi_Strike_effect.png/250px-Bea_Machamp_G-Max_Chi_Strike_effect.png" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="250" height="141" class="mw-file-element" srcset="https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/1/13/Bea_Machamp_G-Max_Chi_Strike_effect.png/375px-Bea_Machamp_G-Max_Chi_Strike_effect.png 1.5x, https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/1/13/Bea_Machamp_G-Max_Chi_Strike_effect.png/500px-Bea_Machamp_G-Max_Chi_Strike_effect.png 2x" data-file-width="1280" data-file-height="720"></a><figcaption>The enhancements that <a href="/wiki/Bea" title="Bea">Bea</a>'s <a href="/wiki/Machamp_(Pok%C3%A9mon)" title="Machamp (Pokémon)">Machamp</a> received from <a href="/wiki/G-Max_Chi_Strike_(move)" title="G-Max Chi Strike (move)">G-Max Chi Strike</a>'s effects</figcaption></figure>
<h3><span id="Pok.C3.A9mon_the_Series"></span><span class="mw-headline" id="Pokémon_the_Series"><i>Pokémon the Series</i></span></h3>
<h4><span id="Pok.C3.A9mon_the_Series:_The_Beginning"></span><span class="mw-headline" id="Pokémon_the_Series:_The_Beginning"><a href="/wiki/Original_series" title="Original series"><i>Pokémon the Series: The Beginning</i></a></span></h4>
<p>In <i><a href="/wiki/EP073" title="EP073">Bad To The Bone</a></i>, <a href="/wiki/Otoshi" title="Otoshi">Otoshi</a>'s <a href="/wiki/Marowak_(Pok%C3%A9mon)" title="Marowak (Pokémon)">Marowak</a> used <a href="/wiki/Focus_Energy_(move)" title="Focus Energy (move)">Focus Energy</a> to heighten its chances of landing a critical hit, which it did when it knocked <a href="/wiki/Ash%27s_Bulbasaur" title="Ash's Bulbasaur">Ash's Bulbasaur</a> out with a single <a href="/wiki/Bone_Club_(move)" title="Bone Club (move)">Bone Club</a> attack. <a href="/wiki/Jessie%27s_Arbok" title="Jessie's Arbok">Jessie's Arbok</a> also took a critical hit from Marowak in the same fashion.
</p>
<h4><span id="Pok.C3.A9mon_the_Series:_Ruby_and_Sapphire"></span><span class="mw-headline" id="Pokémon_the_Series:_Ruby_and_Sapphire"><a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_the_Series:_Ruby_and_Sapphire" title="Pokémon the Series: Ruby and Sapphire"><i>Pokémon the Series: Ruby and Sapphire</i></a></span></h4>
<p>In the Japanese version of <i><a href="/wiki/AG127" title="AG127">From Brags to Riches</a></i>, <a href="/wiki/Morrison" title="Morrison">Morrison</a>'s <a href="/wiki/Gligar_(Pok%C3%A9mon)" title="Gligar (Pokémon)">Gligar</a>'s <a href="/wiki/Guillotine_(move)" title="Guillotine (move)">Guillotine</a> was referred to as a critical hit when it defeated <a href="/wiki/Gavin" title="Gavin">Gavin</a>'s <a href="/wiki/Machamp_(Pok%C3%A9mon)" title="Machamp (Pokémon)">Machamp</a>, despite the fact that a <a href="/wiki/One-hit_knockout_move" title="One-hit knockout move">one-hit knockout move</a> can never land a critical hit. This was corrected in the English <a href="/wiki/Dub" title="Dub">dub</a>.
</p><p>In <i><a href="/wiki/AG128" title="AG128">Shocks and Bonds</a></i>, during <a href="/wiki/Ash_Ketchum" title="Ash Ketchum">Ash</a>'s match against <a href="/wiki/Clark" title="Clark">Clark</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Ever_Grande_Conference" title="Ever Grande Conference">Ever Grande Conference</a>, <a href="/wiki/Ash%27s_Glalie" title="Ash's Glalie">Ash's Glalie</a> defeated Clark's <a href="/wiki/Charizard_(Pok%C3%A9mon)" title="Charizard (Pokémon)">Charizard</a> with a critical hit from <a href="/wiki/Headbutt_(move)" title="Headbutt (move)">Headbutt</a>, giving Ash the victory.
</p><p>In <i><a href="/wiki/AG130" title="AG130">Choose It or Lose It!</a></i>, during Ash's <a href="/wiki/Full_Battle" title="Full Battle">Full Battle</a> against Morrison in the Victory Tournament portion of the Ever Grande Conference, <a href="/wiki/Ash%27s_Corphish" title="Ash's Corphish">Ash's Corphish</a> knocked Morrison's <a href="/wiki/Growlithe_(Pok%C3%A9mon)" title="Growlithe (Pokémon)">Growlithe</a> out with a critical hit from <a href="/wiki/Crabhammer_(move)" title="Crabhammer (move)">Crabhammer</a>.
</p><p>In <i><a href="/wiki/AG187" title="AG187">The Unbeatable Lightness of Seeing!</a></i>, during <a href="/wiki/May_(anime)" title="May (anime)">May</a>'s battle against <a href="/wiki/Drew" title="Drew">Drew</a>, both Drew's <a href="/wiki/Drew%27s_Roselia" class="mw-redirect" title="Drew's Roselia">Roselia</a> and <a href="/wiki/Drew%27s_Butterfree" class="mw-redirect" title="Drew's Butterfree">Butterfree</a> knocked May's <a href="/wiki/May%27s_Combusken" class="mw-redirect" title="May's Combusken">Combusken</a> and <a href="/wiki/May%27s_Beautifly" title="May's Beautifly">Beautifly</a> out with a critical hit from their respective <a href="/wiki/Solar_Beam_(move)" title="Solar Beam (move)">Solar Beam</a> and <a href="/wiki/Psybeam_(move)" title="Psybeam (move)">Psybeam</a> attacks.
</p>
<h4><span id="Pok.C3.A9mon_the_Series:_Diamond_and_Pearl"></span><span class="mw-headline" id="Pokémon_the_Series:_Diamond_and_Pearl"><a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_the_Series:_Diamond_and_Pearl" title="Pokémon the Series: Diamond and Pearl"><i>Pokémon the Series: Diamond and Pearl</i></a></span></h4>
<p>In <i><a href="/wiki/DP034" title="DP034">Buizel Your Way Out Of This!</a></i>, <a href="/wiki/Dawn%27s_Piplup" title="Dawn's Piplup">Dawn's Piplup</a> used <a href="/wiki/Bubble_Beam_(move)" title="Bubble Beam (move)">Bubble Beam</a> to land a critical hit on a wild <a href="/wiki/Dawn%27s_Buizel" class="mw-redirect" title="Dawn's Buizel">Buizel</a> and <a href="/wiki/Fainting" title="Fainting">knock him out</a> before <a href="/wiki/Catching" class="mw-redirect" title="Catching">catching</a> him.
</p><p>In <i><a href="/wiki/DP118" title="DP118">Pursuing a Lofty Goal!</a></i>, during the second match in the <a href="/wiki/Squallville_Pok%C3%A9Ringer" title="Squallville PokéRinger">Squallville PokéRinger</a>, <a href="/wiki/Paul" title="Paul">Paul</a>'s <a href="/wiki/Paul%27s_Honchkrow" title="Paul's Honchkrow">Honchkrow</a> used <a href="/wiki/Sky_Attack_(move)" title="Sky Attack (move)">Sky Attack</a> in conjunction with its <a href="/wiki/Super_Luck_(Ability)" title="Super Luck (Ability)">Super Luck</a> <a href="/wiki/Ability" title="Ability">Ability</a> to land a critical hit on <a href="/wiki/Provo" title="Provo">Provo</a>'s <a href="/wiki/Dragonite_(Pok%C3%A9mon)" title="Dragonite (Pokémon)">Dragonite</a> and knock it out.
</p><p>In <i><a href="/wiki/DP172" title="DP172">With the Easiest of Grace!</a></i>, <a href="/wiki/Dawn%27s_Togekiss" title="Dawn's Togekiss">Dawn's Togekiss</a> used <a href="/wiki/Air_Slash_(move)" title="Air Slash (move)">Air Slash</a> to land a critical hit on <a href="/wiki/Jessie%27s_Yanmega" title="Jessie's Yanmega">Jessie's Yanmega</a> and knock her out.
</p>
<h4><span id="Pok.C3.A9mon_the_Series:_Black_.26_White"></span><span class="mw-headline" id="Pokémon_the_Series:_Black_&_White"><a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_the_Series:_Black_%26_White" title="Pokémon the Series: Black & White"><i>Pokémon the Series: Black & White</i></a></span></h4>
<p>In <i><a href="/wiki/BW010" title="BW010">A Rival Battle for Club Champ!</a></i>, <a href="/wiki/Trip" title="Trip">Trip</a>'s <a href="/wiki/Tranquill_(Pok%C3%A9mon)" title="Tranquill (Pokémon)">Tranquill</a> used <a href="/wiki/Aerial_Ace_(move)" title="Aerial Ace (move)">Aerial Ace</a> in conjunction with its Super Luck Ability to knock <a href="/wiki/Ash%27s_Oshawott" title="Ash's Oshawott">Ash's Oshawott</a> out in one critical hit. Later on in the match, Tranquill defeated <a href="/wiki/Ash%27s_Tepig" class="mw-redirect" title="Ash's Tepig">Tepig</a> in the same manner, this time having its damage also boosted by <a href="/wiki/Work_Up_(move)" title="Work Up (move)">Work Up</a>.
</p><p>In <i><a href="/wiki/BW072" title="BW072">A Clubsplosion of Excitement!</a></i>, during the first round of the <a href="/wiki/Clubsplosion" title="Clubsplosion">Clubsplosion</a>, <a href="/wiki/Bianca%27s_Emboar" title="Bianca's Emboar">Bianca's Emboar</a> knocked Trip's <a href="/wiki/Conkeldurr_(Pok%C3%A9mon)" title="Conkeldurr (Pokémon)">Conkeldurr</a> out in one critical hit by <a href="/wiki/Fling_(move)" title="Fling (move)">Flinging</a> its own pillars at it.
</p>
<h4><span id="Pok.C3.A9mon_Journeys:_The_Series"></span><span class="mw-headline" id="Pokémon_Journeys:_The_Series"><a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Journeys:_The_Series" title="Pokémon Journeys: The Series"><i>Pokémon Journeys: The Series</i></a></span></h4>
<p>In <i><a href="/wiki/JN060" title="JN060">Beyond Chivalry… Aiming to be a Leek Master!</a></i>, during a <a href="/wiki/World_Coronation_Series" title="World Coronation Series">World Coronation Series</a> <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_battle" title="Pokémon battle">battle</a>, Ash's <a href="/wiki/Farfetch%27d_(Pok%C3%A9mon)" title="Farfetch'd (Pokémon)">Farfetch'd</a> landed three critical hits on <a href="/wiki/Rinto" title="Rinto">Rinto</a>'s <a href="/wiki/Gallade_(Pok%C3%A9mon)" title="Gallade (Pokémon)">Gallade</a> with <a href="/wiki/Fury_Cutter_(move)" title="Fury Cutter (move)">Fury Cutter</a>, causing the <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_category" title="Pokémon category">Wild Duck Pokémon</a> to evolve into a <a href="/wiki/Ash%27s_Sirfetch%27d" title="Ash's Sirfetch'd">Sirfetch'd</a>.
</p><p>In <i><a href="/wiki/JN086" title="JN086">A Battle of Mega Versus Max!</a></i>, <a href="/wiki/Bea" title="Bea">Bea</a>'s <a href="/wiki/Gigantamax" title="Gigantamax">Gigantamax</a> Machamp attacked Ash's <a href="/wiki/Mega_Evolution" title="Mega Evolution">Mega</a> <a href="/wiki/Ash%27s_Lucario" title="Ash's Lucario">Lucario</a> with <a href="/wiki/G-Max_Chi_Strike_(move)" title="G-Max Chi Strike (move)">G-Max Chi Strike</a>. While Mega Lucario survived long enough for Machamp to turn back to normal, it retained the enhancements that it received from using its <a href="/wiki/Signature_move" title="Signature move">signature</a> <a href="/wiki/G-Max_Move" title="G-Max Move">G-Max Move</a>, allowing it to pinpoint Mega Lucario's weak points.
</p><p>In <i><a href="/wiki/JN129" title="JN129">A Flood of Torrential Gains!</a></i>, <a href="/wiki/Leon_(anime)" title="Leon (anime)">Leon</a>'s <a href="/wiki/Inteleon_(Pok%C3%A9mon)" title="Inteleon (Pokémon)">Inteleon</a> landed a critical hit on <a href="/wiki/Ash%27s_Gengar" title="Ash's Gengar">Ash's Gengar</a> with <a href="/wiki/Dark_Pulse_(move)" title="Dark Pulse (move)">Dark Pulse</a> during their <a href="/wiki/Masters_Eight_Tournament" title="Masters Eight Tournament">Masters Eight Tournament</a> battle, resulting in Gengar's Gigantamax state ending prematurely.
</p>
<div id="AdThrive_Content_4_desktop" class="adthrive-ad adthrive-content adthrive-content-4 adthrive-ad-cls" style="min-height: 250px;"></div><h3><span id="Pok.C3.A9mon_Horizons:_The_Series"></span><span class="mw-headline" id="Pokémon_Horizons:_The_Series"><i>Pokémon Horizons: The Series</i></span></h3>
<p>In <i><a href="/wiki/HZ130" title="HZ130">Hamber's Moonlight Battle</a></i>, <a href="/wiki/Chalce" title="Chalce">Chalce</a>'s Mega <a href="/wiki/Medicham_(Pok%C3%A9mon)" title="Medicham (Pokémon)">Medicham</a> landed a critical hit on <a href="/wiki/Hamber" title="Hamber">Hamber</a>'s <a href="/wiki/List_of_Pok%C3%A9mon_with_form_differences#Ursaluna" title="List of Pokémon with form differences">Bloodmoon</a> <a href="/wiki/Ursaluna_(Pok%C3%A9mon)" title="Ursaluna (Pokémon)">Ursaluna</a> with an <a href="/wiki/Axe_Kick_(move)" title="Axe Kick (move)">Axe Kick</a>, knocking him out.
</p>
